name: The Silverhymn Mine
history: Established several decades before the War of Broken Banners, the Silverhymn Mine was once a modest but productive independent mining operation. Its miners occasionally uncovered peculiar crystalline formations that resonated when struck. As the workings extended deeper into the mountain, the miners breached chambers of considerably greater antiquity. Following unexplained accidents and the collapse of its principal entrance, the mine was abandoned.
current_state: The upper workings have remained largely undisturbed for years. At night a low, melodic sound occasionally emanates from the mountainside. Prospectors have recently observed smoke rising from a sealed ventilation shaft. A small Blackforge Consortium surveying party has entered the lower workings from an ancient subterranean passage to investigate the crystalline deposits.
inhabitants: Ordinary cave-dwelling creatures in the upper workings; a small duergar surveying party in the lower chambers, without a permanent presence.
danger_level: Moderate in the upper workings; greater in the deeper chambers. Potentially suitable for an early expedition if approached cautiously.
discovery: A secluded ravine in the eastern mountain foothills. A disused mining trail beyond the Old Camp leads to the collapsed entrance. Former miners, prospectors, and Blackpick families know portions of its history.
related_plots: P-001 — The Iron Price (indirect); P-010 — The Breaking of the Anvil (potential).
site_type: mine | Abandoned infrastructure | Abandoned silver mine; ancient subterranean ruins
points_of_interest:
Abandoned miners’ quarters; collapsed entrance; concealed ventilation shaft; resonant crystal galleries; an ancient dwarven chamber surrounding an immense crystalline formation; a passage beyond the known workings.

Unresolved elements: Original purpose of the crystalline chamber; cause of the accidents; properties of the crystals; destination of the passage; extent of the duergar’s knowledge.
